groups.title: Tracker fields
rows: Calendar month assigned to the record.
Displayed as mmm yyyy; used for chronological reporting.
Date the customer email or JIRA item was received or logged.
Use a true Excel date in dd-mmm-yyyy format.
Operational event category associated with the record.
Select the closest standard event category.
Customer account that raised or is associated with the record.
Use the agreed customer name consistently.
Count of customer accounts affected or represented.
Whole number; normally 1 unless multiple customers are combined.
Title identifying the event, bulletin, or customer query.
Whether the record is a complaint or an inquiry.
Complaint indicates a service concern; Inquiry requests information or verification.
Customer-facing description of what prompted the record.
Use the most specific reason label supported by the facts.
Detailed cause or handling category beneath Root Cause.
Use the category that best describes the failure mechanism.
Classifies the response as an enhancement or defect correction.
Improvement enhances controls; Bug indicates a product defect.
Fixed, RCA Shared, or Clarification Provided.
Specific automation or control proposed for the case.
Free-text action; use standardized wording where possible.
Indicates whether a root cause analysis was requested.
Concise factual summary of the issue, finding, and action.
Must support the Reason, Root Cause, status, and automation fields.
May contain duration text or a Yes/No legacy value.
Indicates whether expected EventWatch coverage, alerting, or WarRoom action was missed.
Yes only for an actual miss; No for clarification, relevancy, or mapping-only cases.
Numeric month order used for sorting.
Keep numeric for SLA analysis; blank when not measured.
Standard month date used for dashboard aggregation.
True Excel month date formatted mmm yyyy.
Business impact or operational priority level.
Normalized automation theme used for dashboard reporting.
Select one of the approved focus categories.
Atlassian issue key linking the record to the ticket that tracks it.
EAO-<n> for the EventWatch_AI_Ops project; older records may carry DATA, TS, BI or TENAR keys. Blank where no ticket was raised.
Root cause summary for the record, taken from the RCA shared on the linked Jira ticket.

Free text. Blank where no RCA was requested or none has been issued yet. Where the RCA went out only as a PDF attachment the entry says so, rather than paraphrasing a document that is not in the ticket.
Which team the record is directed to for action.

EventWatch Ops - Nitin Rindhe for People- and Process-rooted records: analyst judgement, escalation, WarRoom decisions, threshold and methodology questions. Product & Platform for Product-rooted records: ingestion, source coverage, keyword, clustering, mapping, visibility, platform and automation defects. Derived from Root Cause. EventWatch Ops still owns the customer-facing RCA on Product-routed records; routing says who investigates, not who replies.

groups.title: Issue types
rows: Customer reports a service failure, miss, delay, incorrect action, or other concern.
Customer requests verification, explanation, or information without a confirmed service failure.

groups.title: Event types
rows: Formal insolvency, bankruptcy filing, restructuring, or equivalent proceeding.
Release or leak of a hazardous chemical substance.
Cybersecurity incident such as ransomware, intrusion, compromise, or data breach.
Seismic event with potential operational or supply-chain impact.
Severe weather such as storms, flooding, drought, heat, or snowstorms. Tornado and Hurricane/Typhoon are separate categories and take precedence.
Planned or unplanned closure of a manufacturing facility.
Operational interruption at a manufacturing facility that is not classified as closure or fire.
Fire affecting a manufacturing, production, or storage facility.
Material financial difficulty that does not yet constitute a formal bankruptcy event.
Political, border, security, conflict, or humanitarian development affecting operations.
Strike, work stoppage, industrial action, or labor-related disruption.
Change in senior executive or organizational leadership.
Merger, acquisition, divestiture, or comparable corporate transaction.
Demonstration, civil unrest, riot, or blockade driven by protest activity.
Government rule, sanction, export control, or regulatory action.
Shortage or constrained availability of materials, components, energy, or goods.
Disruption to roads, bridges, ports, rail, air, or logistics routes.
Uncontrolled vegetation fire with potential geographic or operational impact.
Tropical cyclone classified as a hurricane or typhoon, with potential geographic, operational, or supply-chain impact.
Use specifically for hurricanes and typhoons rather than the broader Extreme Weather category.
Counterfeit, grey-market, or otherwise non-genuine goods entering the supply chain.
Standard event category. Covers counterfeit-risk intelligence and advisory requests as well as confirmed incidents.
Lawsuit, legal proceeding, or enforcement action involving a supplier or customer-linked entity.
Standard event category. Use where the legal action itself is the event; use Regulatory Change for a rule, sanction, or export-control change.
Defect in what the EventWatch platform presents rather than an event in the outside world: irrelevant, unrecognized, or incorrectly displayed records reaching the customer.
Standard event category. Use when the complaint concerns platform content or data quality, not an external event.
Loss or failure of electrical power supply affecting a facility, region, or grid.
Standard event category. Use for grid and utility failures; use Extreme Weather where the outage is incidental to a storm already being reported.
Tornado with potential geographic, operational, or supply-chain impact.
Standard event category. A tornado event is typed here, not under Extreme Weather; the two are deliberately separate.

groups.title: Root causes
rows: Human judgment, review, prioritization, publishing, or execution was the primary cause.
Policy, workflow, threshold, mapping method, or procedural design was the primary cause.
Technology, data ingestion, source coverage, detection, clustering, or platform behavior was the primary cause.

groups.title: Sub-types
rows: Relevant information entered the workflow later than required.
Related content was split into duplicate WarRooms or event records.
The relevant event was not recognized or converted into reportable coverage.
An incorrect or missing industry classification affected tracking.
Search or detection terms required addition or refinement.
Customer, supplier, company, facility, or impact relationship was missing or incorrect.
A rule, threshold, or decision logic produced or explained the outcome.
A detected item was not handled with the required urgency.
The case required explanation of policy, thresholds, or workflow rather than defect correction.
The item’s relevance to the customer or EventWatch scope was disputed or incorrectly assessed.
Human assessment or quality review led to the issue.
The relevant source was unavailable, unmonitored, restricted, or not harvested.
The concern relates to reporting or consolidation strategy.
A required category or industry tag was missing or incorrect.
Published content was not visible because of profile, portal, notification, or display conditions.
A required WarRoom was not created despite available EventWatch coverage.

groups.title: Severity levels
rows: Material impact or priority requiring elevated management attention.
Standard operational complaint or issue requiring tracked response.
Limited-impact inquiry or quality issue with lower operational urgency.

groups.title: Fix statuses
rows: The root cause analysis was completed and shared with the customer.
The customer received an explanation, verification result, or policy/process clarification.
The linked Jira ticket is still open; no fix, RCA, or clarification has yet been issued to the customer.

groups.title: Improvement vs bug
rows: Control, workflow, model, or monitoring enhancement rather than correction of a confirmed defect.
Confirmed product or engineering defect requiring correction.

groups.title: Flags
rows: A formal root cause analysis was requested.
No formal root cause analysis was requested.
Expected coverage, alerting, escalation, or WarRoom action was missed or materially delayed.
No confirmed reporting miss; the case concerns clarification, relevancy, mapping, duplication, or another non-miss issue.

groups.title: Automation focus
rows: Automate or improve impact-area creation and location validation.
Automatically assign and validate industry classifications.
Detect duplicate/split clusters and preserve one coherent event sequence.
Identify, onboard, and monitor new or missing sources dynamically.
Resolve company, facility, supplier, and customer relationships accurately.
Expand and maintain detection terms across languages and regional variations.
Monitor whether published alerts and WarRooms are visible and delivered to the customer.
Automation that does not fit another standardized focus category.
Validate impact decisions, escalation, publishing, and WarRoom creation.

groups.title: Operational terms
rows: Operational monitoring service that identifies, assesses, and reports events relevant to customers.
Central event workspace used to publish, organize, and update an operational event.
Root Cause Analysis; a documented explanation of why an issue occurred and the corrective/preventive actions.
Non-Conformance; an internal quality record raised when required process or control performance was not met.
Review outcome indicating that available evidence did not meet the threshold for EventWatch escalation.
Automated collection of articles or reports from monitored information sources.
Availability and monitoring of relevant websites, feeds, registries, or publications.
Addition or refinement of search terms when available content was not identified correctly.
Geographic impact logic used to associate an event area with customer or supplier locations.
Grouping of related articles or bulletins into one event record or WarRoom.
Analyst review that validates automated detection and decides whether to escalate or publish.
Customer-mapped supplier assessed as potentially affected by an event.
